How to read this

  1. Rows expand. Click anywhere on a row for the official title, every central contact, the study official or PI with affiliation, and the list of US site cities. Click again to close.
  2. Central contact is the sponsor's registered contact on ClinicalTrials.gov, shown as listed there (name, email, phone). Emails and phones are click-to-send / click-to-dial. Where none is registered the row says so and links to the study record, which carries site-level contacts.
  3. Search covers sponsor, drug, NCT number, indication, study title, contact names and emails, officials, US cities, states and site hospitals. Several words narrow (AND). The sidebar Site location box does the same restricted to places, so you can search a disease up top and a metro on the side.
  4. Sorting is the dropdown: no sort keeps registry order (newest updates first); the other eleven orderings run both directions on every numeric column, and the sorted column is highlighted in the header.
  5. Filters are OR inside a group and AND across groups. Counts beside each option update to reflect the other filters and any search text you have on. Active filters show as chips above the table; click a chip to remove it. Filters, search and sort are written into the URL, so a link to the current view can be shared.
  6. Source. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, pulled 15 Sep 2026: interventional, Phase 2 (including 1/2 and 2/3), industry lead sponsor, at least one US site, status recruiting or not yet recruiting. Enrollment and site counts are the sponsor's registered figures. Per site is enrollment divided by US site count; 405 of 1,046 trials sit above 20 patients per site, roughly where timelines start slipping.

Two honesty notes. The rare-disease flag is keyword matching on indication text, not a curated ontology. Company size is not a lookup: "larger company" is a hand-flagged list of 197 sponsors; the rest are assumed clinical-stage rather than verified.

Coverage: 1,046 of the 1,058 qualifying trials (98.9%). 979 of the 1,046 list a central contact; the rest link out to site contacts. Search and the location box need scripts, so they run on the hosted page but not inside a Claude artifact preview.
